1 tn The phrase &quot;a dry piece of bread&quot; is like bread without butter, a morsel of bread not dipped in vinegar mix (e.g., Ruth 2:14). It represents here a simple, humble meal. 2 tn Heb &quot;and quietness in it&quot;; the construction functions as a circumstantial clause: &quot;in which there is quietness&quot; or &quot;with quietness.&quot; sn The Hebrew word means &quot;quietness&quot; or &quot;ease.&quot; It represents a place where there can be carefree ease because of the sense of peace and security. The Greek rendering suggests that those translators read it as &quot;peace.&quot; Even if the fare is poor, this kind of setting is to be preferred. 3 tn The house is described as being full of &quot;sacrifices of strife&quot; (זִבְחֵי־רִיב, zivkhi-riv). The use of &quot;sacrifices&quot; suggests a connection with the temple (as in 7:14) in which the people may have made their sacrifices and had a large amount meat left over. It is also possible that the reference is simply to a sumptuous meal (Deut 12:15; Isa 34:6; Ezek 39:17). It would be rare for Israelites to eat meat apart from festivals, however. In the construction the genitive could be classified as a genitive of effect, the feast in general &quot;bringing about strife,&quot; or it could simply be an attributive genitive, &quot;a feast characterized by strife.&quot; Abundance often brings deterioration of moral and ethical standards as well as an increase in envy and strife.

4 sn The setting is in the ancient world where a servant rarely advanced beyond his or her station in life. But there are notable exceptions (e.g., Gen 15:3 where the possibility is mentioned, 1 Chr 2:35 where it changed through marriage, and 2 Sam 16:1-4; 19:24-30, with the story of Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth). This proverb focuses on a servant who is wise, one who uses all his abilities effectively - a Joseph figure. 5 sn The parallelism indicates that &quot;ruling over&quot; and &quot;sharing in the inheritance&quot; means that the disgraceful son will be disinherited. 6 tn Heb &quot;son.&quot; 7 tn The form מֵבִישׁ (mevish) is a Hiphil participle, modifying בֵן (ben). This original heir would then be one who caused shame or disgrace to the family, probably by showing a complete lack of wisdom in the choices he made. 8 tn Heb &quot;in the midst of the brothers&quot;; NIV &quot;as one of the brothers.&quot;

9 sn The noun מַצְרֵף (matsref) means &quot;a place or instrument for refining&quot; (cf. ASV, NASB &quot;the refining pot&quot;). The related verb, which means &quot;to melt, refine, smelt,&quot; is used in scripture literally for refining and figuratively for the Lord&apos;s purifying and cleansing and testing people. 10 tn The term &quot;refining&quot; does not appear in the Hebrew text, but is implied by the parallelism; it is supplied in the translation for the sake of clarity. 11 sn The term כּוּר (cur) describes a &quot;furnace&quot; or &quot;smelting pot.&quot; It can be used figuratively for the beneficial side of affliction (Isa 48:10). 12 tn Heb &quot;and.&quot; Most English versions treat this as an adversative (&quot;but&quot;). 13 sn The participle בֹּחֵן (bokhen, &quot;tests&quot;) in this emblematic parallelism takes on the connotations of the crucible and the furnace. When the Lord &quot;tests&quot; human hearts, the test, whatever form it takes, is designed to improve the value of the one being tested. Evil and folly will be removed when such testing takes place.

1 tn The Niphal participle functions substantively and has a reflexive nuance: &quot;one who has separated himself&quot; (cf. KJV, ASV, NASB). He is not merely anti-social; he is a problem for society since he will defy sound judgment. The Mishnah uses the verse to teach the necessity of being part of a community because people have social responsibilities and need each other (m. Avot 2:4). 2 tc The MT has &quot;seeks [his own] desire[s].&quot; The translation in the LXX represents a Hebrew Vorlage of לְתֹאֲנָה (lÿto&apos;anah) instead of לְתַאֲוָה (lÿta&apos;avah); this could be translated &quot;seeks his own occasion,&quot; that is, &quot;his own pretext&quot; (C. H. Toy, Proverbs [ICC], 354; cf. NAB). The MT makes sense as it stands and the emendation is not really necessary. 3 tn Heb &quot;breaks out&quot;; NRSV &quot;showing contempt for&quot;; NLT &quot;snarling at.&quot; This individual breaks out in contention against sound judgment. He is in opposition to society (e.g., Prov 17:14; 20:3).

4 sn This expression forms an understatement (tapeinosis); the opposite is the point - he detests understanding or discernment. 5 tn The Hitpael infinitive construct בְּהִתְגַּלּוֹת (bÿhitgalot) functions nominally as the object of the preposition. The term means &quot;reveal, uncover, betray.&quot; So the fool takes pleasure &quot;in uncovering&quot; his heart. 6 tn Heb &quot;his heart.&quot; This is a metonymy meaning &quot;what is on his mind&quot; (cf. NAB &quot;displaying what he thinks&quot;; NRSV &quot;expressing personal opinion&quot;). This kind of person is in love with his own ideas and enjoys spewing them out (W. McKane, Proverbs [OTL], 515). It is the kind of person who would ask a question, not to learn, but to show everyone how clever he is (cf. TEV).

7 tc The MT has &quot;a wicked [person].&quot; Many commentators emend the text to רֶשַׁע (resha&apos;, &quot;wickedness&quot;) which makes better parallelism with &quot;shame&quot; (W. McKane, Proverbs [OTL], 521; R. B. Y. Scott, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes [AB], 112; C. H. Toy, Proverbs [ICC], 355; cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV). However, there is no external evidence for this emendation. 8 sn &quot;Contempt&quot; (בּוּז, buz) accompanies the wicked; &quot;reproach&quot; (חֶרְפָּה, kherpah) goes with shame. This reproach refers to the critical rebukes and taunts of the community against a wicked person. 9 tn The term &quot;comes&quot; does not appear in the Hebrew but is supplied in the translation for the sake of clarity and smoothness.

1 sn People should follow honesty even if it leads to poverty (e.g., Prov 18:23; 19:22). 2 tn Heb &quot;lips.&quot; The term &quot;lips&quot; is a metonymy for what one says with his lips. The expression &quot;perverse in his lips&quot; refers to speech that is morally perverted. Some medieval Hebrew mss, the Syriac, and Tg. Prov 19:1 have &quot;his ways&quot; rather than &quot;his lips&quot; (e.g., Prov 28:6); cf. NAB. 3 tc The Syriac and Tg. Prov 19:1 read &quot;rich&quot; instead of MT &quot;fool.&quot; This makes tighter antithetical parallelism than MT and is followed by NAB. However, the MT makes sense as it stands; this is an example of metonymical parallelism. The MT reading is also supported by the LXX. The Hebrew construction uses וְהוּא (vÿhu&apos;), &quot;and he [is],&quot; before &quot;fool.&quot; This may be rendered &quot;one who is perverse while a fool&quot; or &quot;a fool at the same time.&quot;

4 tn Heb &quot;not good.&quot; This is a figure known as tapeinosis (a deliberate understatement to emphasize a worst-case scenario): &quot;it is dangerous!&quot; 5 tn The interpretation of this line depends largely on the meaning of נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) which has a broad range of meanings: (1) the breathing substance of man, (2) living being, (3) life, (4) person, (5) seat of the appetites, (6) seat of emotions and passions, (7) activities of intellect, emotion and will, (8) moral character, etc. (BDB 659-61 s.v.). In light of the synonymous parallelism, the most likely nuance here is &quot;zeal, passion&quot; (HALOT 713 s.v. 8). NIV takes the word in the sense of &quot;vitality&quot; and &quot;drive&quot; - &quot;it is not good to have zeal without knowledge&quot; (cf. NCV, TEV, and NLT which are all similar). 6 tn Heb &quot;he who is hasty with his feet.&quot; The verb אוּץ (&apos;uts) means &quot;to be pressed; to press; to make haste.&quot; The verb is followed by the preposition בְּ (bet) which indicates that with which one hastens - his feet. The word &quot;feet&quot; is a synecdoche of part for the whole person - body and mind working together (cf. NLT &quot;a person who moves too quickly&quot;). 7 tn Heb &quot;misses the goal.&quot; The participle חוֹטֵא (khote&apos;) can be translated &quot;sins&quot; (cf. KJV, ASV), but in this context it refers only to actions without knowledge, which could lead to sin, or could lead simply to making poor choices (cf. NAB &quot;blunders&quot;; NASB &quot;errs&quot;; NCV &quot;might make a mistake&quot;). sn The basic meaning of the verb is &quot;to miss a goal or the way.&quot; D. Kidner says, &quot;How negative is the achievement of a man who wants tangible and quick rewards&quot; - he will miss the way (Proverbs [TOTC], 132).

8 tn Heb &quot;the folly of a man.&quot; 9 tn The verb סָלַף (salaf) normally means &quot;to twist; to pervert; to overturn,&quot; but in this context it means &quot;to subvert&quot; (BDB 701 s.v.); cf. ASV &quot;subverteth.&quot; sn J. H. Greenstone comments: &quot;Man&apos;s own failures are the result of his own folly and should not be attributed to God&quot; (Proverbs, 201). 10 tn The clause begins with vav on the nonverb phrase &quot;against the Lord.&quot; While clause structure and word order is less compelling in a book like Proverbs, this fits well as a circumstantial clause indicating concession. 11 sn The &quot;heart raging&quot; is a metonymy of cause (or adjunct); it represents the emotions that will lead to blaming God for the frustration. Genesis 42:28 offers a calmer illustration of this as the brothers ask what God was doing to them.

1 sn The drinks are wine and barley beer (e.g., Lev 10:9; Deut 14:26; Isa 28:7). These terms here could be understood as personifications, but better as metonymies for those who drink wine and beer. The inebriated person mocks and brawls. 2 tn The two participles לֵץ (lets, &quot;mocker&quot;) and הֹמֶה (homeh, &quot;brawler&quot;) are substantives; they function as predicates in the sentence. Excessive use of intoxicants excites the drinker to boisterous behavior and aggressive attitudes - it turns them into mockers and brawlers. 3 sn The proverb does not prohibit the use of wine or beer; in fact, strong drink was used at festivals and celebrations. But intoxication was considered out of bounds for a member of the covenant community (e.g., 23:20-21, 29-35; 31:4-7). To be led astray by their use is not wise.

4 tn Heb &quot;the terror of a king&quot; (so ASV, NASB); The term &quot;terror&quot; is a metonymy of effect for cause: the anger of a king that causes terror among the people. The term &quot;king&quot; functions as a possessive genitive: &quot;a king&apos;s anger&quot; (cf. NIV &quot;A king&apos;s wrath&quot;; NLT &quot;The king&apos;s fury&quot;). 5 tn The verb מִתְעַבְּרוֹ (mit&apos;abbÿro) is problematic; in the MT the form is the Hitpael participle with a pronominal suffix, which is unusual, for the direct object of this verb usually takes a preposition first: &quot;is angry with.&quot; The LXX rendered it &quot;angers [or, irritates].&quot; 6 sn The expression &quot;sins against himself&quot; has been taken by some to mean &quot;forfeits his life&quot; (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV) or &quot;endangers his life&quot; (cf. NCV, NLT). That may be the implication of getting oneself in trouble with an angry king (cf. TEV &quot;making him angry is suicide&quot;).

7 tn Heb &quot;man.&quot; 8 tn Heb &quot;cessation&quot; (שֶׁבֶת, shevet); NAB &quot;to shun strife&quot;; NRSV &quot;refrain from strife.&quot; sn One cannot avoid conflict altogether; but the proverb is instructing that at the first sign of conflict the honorable thing to do is to find a way to end it. 9 tn Heb &quot;breaks out.&quot; The Hitpael of the verb גָּלַע (gala&apos;, &quot;to expose; to lay bare&quot;) means &quot;to break out; to disclose oneself,&quot; and so the idea of flaring up in a quarrel is clear. 1 tn Heb &quot;a name.&quot; The idea of the name being &quot;good&quot; is implied; it has the connotation here of a reputation (cf. TEV, CEV, NLT). 2 tn &quot;To be chosen rather than&quot; is a translation of the Niphal participle with the comparative degree taken into consideration. Cf. CEV &quot;worth much more than.&quot; 3 tn Heb &quot;favor of goodness.&quot; This is a somewhat difficult expression. Some English versions render the phrase &quot;favor is better than silver or gold&quot; (so NASB, NRSV) making it parallel to the first colon. But if &quot;good&quot; is retained as an attributive modifier, then it would mean one was well thought of, or one had engaging qualities (cf. ASV &quot;loving favor; NLT &quot;high esteem&quot;). This fits with the idea of the reputation in the first colon, for a good name would bring with it the favor of others.

4 tn The form of the verb is the Niphal perfect of פָּגַשׁ (pagash); it means &quot;to meet together [or, each other]&quot; (cf. KJV, ASV). The point is that rich and poor live side by side in this life, but they are both part of God&apos;s creation (cf. NAB, NASB &quot;have a common bond&quot;). Some commentators have taken this to mean that they should live together because they are part of God&apos;s creation; but the verb form will not sustain that meaning. 5 tn Heb &quot;all.&quot; The Lord is sovereign over both groups, that is, he has had the final say whether a person is rich or poor. People would do well to treat all people with respect, for God can as easily reduce the rich to poverty as raise up the poor to wealth.

6 sn The contrast is between the &quot;shrewd&quot; (prudent) person and the &quot;simpleton.&quot; The shrewd person knows where the dangers and pitfalls are in life and so can avoid them; the naive person is unwary, untrained, and gullible, unable to survive the dangers of the world and blundering into them. 7 tn Heb &quot;evil,&quot; a term that is broad enough to include (1) &quot;sin&quot; as well as (2) any form of &quot;danger&quot; (NIV, NCV, NRSV, NLT) or &quot;trouble&quot; (TEV, CEV). The second option is more likely what is meant here: The naive simpleton does not see the danger to be avoided and so suffers for it. 8 tn Heb &quot;go on&quot;; the word &quot;right&quot; is supplied in the translation to clarify the meaning: The naive person, oblivious to impending danger, meets it head on (cf. TEV &quot;will walk right into it&quot;). 9 tn The verb עָנַשׁ (&apos;anash) means &quot;to fine&quot; specifically. In the Niphal stem it means &quot;to be fined,&quot; or more generally, &quot;to be punished.&quot; In this line the punishment is the consequence of blundering into trouble - they will pay for it.

1 tn The construction uses the imperfect tense of instruction with the infinitive absolute to emphasize the careful discernment required on such occasions. Cf. NIV &quot;note well&quot;; NLT &quot;pay attention.&quot; 2 tn Or &quot;who,&quot; referring to the ruler (so ASV, NAB, TEV).

3 sn The expression &quot;put a knife to your throat&quot; is an idiom that means &quot;curb your appetite&quot; or &quot;control yourself&quot; (cf. TEV). The instruction was from a time when people dealt with all-powerful tyrants. To enter the presence of such a person and indulge one&apos;s appetites would be to take a very high risk. 4 tn Heb &quot;lord of appetite.&quot; The idiom בַּעַל נֶפֶשׁ (ba&apos;al nefesh) refers to someone who possesses a large appetite (cf. NAB &quot;a ravenous appetite&quot;). A person with a big appetite is in danger of taking liberties when invited to court.

5 tn Heb &quot;his&quot;; the referent (the ruler mentioned in v. 1) has been specified in the translation for clarity. 6 sn The final line gives the causal clause: The impressive feast is not what it appears to be; the king is not doing you a favor, but rather wants something from you or is observing you (K&D 17:104); cf. TEV &quot;he may be trying to trick you.&quot; 7 sn Verses 1-3 form the sixth saying about being cautious before rulers (cf. Instruction of Amememope, chap. 23, 23:13-18). One should not get too familiar with rulers, for they always have ulterior motives. The Mishnah cites Gamaliel as warning that a ruler only draws someone into his court for his purpose, but in their day of trouble he will not be there to help them (m. Abot 2:3).

1 sn This section of the book of Proverbs contains proverbs attributed to Solomon but copied by Hezekiah&apos;s sages (between 715 b.c. and 687 b.c.). Some scholars conclude that this has no historical value other than to report the later disposition that people thought they came from Solomon&apos;s time, but if that were the only consideration, then that in itself would have to be considered as a piece of historical information. But if the reference is an earlier note in the collection, then it becomes more valuable for consideration. The proverbs in these lines differ from the earlier ones in that these are multiple line sayings using more similes; chapters 28-29 are similar to 10-16, but chapters 25-27 differ in having few references to God.

2 sn The proverb provides a contrast between God and the king, and therein is the clue to the range of application involved. The interest of the king is ruling or administering his government; and so the subject matter is a contrast to the way God rules his kingdom. 3 sn The two infinitives form the heart of the contrast - &quot;to conceal a matter&quot; and &quot;to search out a matter.&quot; God&apos;s government of the universe is beyond human understanding - humans cannot begin to fathom the intentions and operations of it. But it is the glory of kings to search out matters and make them intelligible to the people. Human government cannot claim divine secrecy; kings have to study and investigate everything before making a decision, even divine government as far as possible. But kings who rule as God&apos;s representatives must also try to represent his will in human affairs - they must even inquire after God to find his will. This is their glorious nature and responsibility. For more general information on vv. 2-27, see G. E. Bryce, &quot;Another Wisdom &apos;Book&apos; in Proverbs,&quot; JBL 91 (1972): 145-57.

4 tn Heb &quot;heavens for height and earth for depth.&quot; The proverb is clearly intending the first line to be an illustration of the second - it is almost emblematic parallelism. 5 sn The proverb is affirming a simple fact: The king&apos;s plans and decisions are beyond the comprehension of the common people. While the king would make many things clear to the people, there are other things that are &quot;above their heads&quot; or &quot;too deep for them.&quot; They are unsearchable because of his superior wisdom, his caprice, or his need for secrecy. Inscrutability is sometimes necessary to keep a firm grip on power.

1 sn &quot;Honor&quot; in this passage probably means respect, external recognition of worth, accolades, advancement to high position, etc. All of these would be out of place with a fool; so the sage is warning against elevating or acclaiming those who are worthless. See also J. A. Emerton, &quot;Notes on Some Passages in the Book of Proverbs,&quot; VT 15 (1965): 271-79. 2 sn The first twelve verses of this chapter, Prov 26:1-12, are sometimes called &quot;the Book of Fools&quot; because they deal with the actions of fools.

3 tn Heb &quot;causeless curse&quot; (KJV similar) describes an undeserved curse (cf. NIV, NRSV). The Hebrew word translated &quot;causeless&quot; is the adverb from ָחנַן (khanan); it means &quot;without cause; gratuitous.&quot; sn This proverb is saying that a curse that is uttered will be powerless if that curse is undeserved. It was commonly believed in the ancient world that blessings and curses had power in themselves, that once spoken they were effectual. But scripture makes it clear that the power of a blessing or a curse depends on the power of the one behind it (e.g., Num 22:38; 23:8). A curse would only take effect if the one who declared it had the authority to do so, and he would only do that if the curse was deserved. 4 tc The MT has the negative with the verb &quot;to enter; to come&quot; to mean &quot;will not come&quot; (לֹא תָבֹא, lo&apos; tavo&apos;). This is interpreted to mean &quot;will not come to rest&quot; or &quot;will not come home.&quot; Some commentators have taken the Qere reading of לוֹ (lo) instead, and read it as &quot;will come home to him.&quot; This is also a little difficult; but it gives the idea that an undeserved curse will come [back] to him [who gave it]. Just as a bird will fly around and eventually come home, so will the undeserved curse return on the one who gave it. This is plausible; but there is no referent for the suffix, making it syntactically difficult.
5 sn A fool must be disciplined by force like an animal - there is no reasoning. The fool is as difficult to manage as the donkey or horse.

1 tn The form אַל־תִּתְהַלֵּל (&apos;al-tithallel) is the Hitpael jussive negated; it is from the common verb &quot;to praise,&quot; and so in this setting means &quot;to praise oneself&quot; or &quot;to boast.&quot; sn The verse rules out one&apos;s overconfident sense of ability to control the future. No one can presume on the future. 2 sn The word &quot;tomorrow&quot; is a metonymy of subject, meaning what will be done tomorrow, or in the future in general. 3 sn The expression &quot;you do not know&quot; balances the presumption of the first line, reminding the disciple of his ignorance and therefore his need for humility (e.g., Matt 6:34; Luke 12:20; Jas 4:13-16).

4 tn Heb &quot;a stranger.&quot; This does not necessarily refer to a non-Israelite, as has been demonstrated before in the book of Proverbs, but these are people outside the familiar and accepted circles. The point is that such a person would be objective in speaking about your abilities and accomplishments. 5 sn &quot;Mouth&quot; and &quot;lips&quot; are metonymies of cause; they mean &quot;what is said.&quot; People should try to avoid praising themselves. Self praise can easily become a form of pride, even if it begins with trivial things. It does not establish a reputation; reputation comes from what others think about you. 6 tn &quot;a foreigner&quot;; KJV, ASV, NASB, NRSV &quot;a stranger.&quot;

7 tn The subject matter is the vexation produced by a fool. The term כַּעַס (ca&apos;as) means &quot;vexation&quot; (ASV); provocation&quot; (NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); &quot;anger&quot; (KJV &quot;wrath&quot;) and usually refers to undeserved treatment. Cf. NLT &quot;the resentment caused by a fool.&quot; sn The same noun is used in 1 Sam 1:6, 16 for the &quot;provocation&quot; given to Hannah by Peninnah for being barren. 8 sn The contrast is made between dealing with the vexation of a fool and physical labor (moving stones and sand). 1 sn The line portrays the insecurity of a guilty person - he flees because he has a guilty conscience, or because he is suspicious of others around him, or because he fears judgment. 2 tn The verb בָּטַח (batakh) means &quot;to trust; to be secure; to be confident.&quot; Cf. KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT &quot;bold.&quot; sn The righteous, who seek to find favor with God and man, have a clear conscience and do not need to look over their shoulders for avengers or law enforcers. Their position is one of confidence, so that they do not flee.

3 sn The Hebrew word translated &quot;rebellious&quot; has rebellion as its basic meaning, and that is the idea here. The proverb is describing a time when sinfulness brings about social and political unrest. 4 tn Heb &quot;many are its princes&quot; (so NASB). sn In such a chaotic time there will be many rulers, either simultaneously or in a rapid sequence. The times of the judges or the days of the northern kings of Israel provide examples. 5 tn Heb &quot;a man who understands [and] knows&quot;; NRSV &quot;an intelligent ruler&quot;; NLT &quot;wise and knowledgeable leaders.&quot; 6 tc The LXX reads (probably from a different underlying Hebrew text): &quot;It is the fault of a violent man that quarrels start, but they are settled by a man of discernment.&quot; For a survey of suggestions, see C. H. Toy, Proverbs (ICC), 495, and W. McKane, Proverbs (OTL), 630. tn This last line is difficult. The MT has כֵּן יַאֲרִיךְ (ken ya&apos;arikh). The verb means &quot;to prolong,&quot; but כֵּן (ken) is open to several possibilities for meaning. J. H. Greenstone&apos;s interpretation of it as a noun from the Hollow root כּוּן (kun) with a meaning of &quot;established order&quot; is what is expected here (Proverbs, 293). sn For a study of the verses in chapters 28 and 29 concerning kings and governments, see B. V. Malchow, &quot;A Manual for Future Monarchs,&quot; CBQ 47 (1985): 238-45.

7 tc The MT reads &quot;a poor man,&quot; גֶּבֶר רָשׁ (gever rash); cf. KJV, NASB, NLT. The problem is that the poor in the book of Proverbs is not an oppressor and does not have the power to be such. So commentators assume the word is incorrect. By a slight change to רָשָׁע (rasha&apos;) the reading becomes &quot;a wicked ruler&quot; [Heb &quot;a wicked mighty man&quot;]. There is no textual support for this change. The LXX, however, reads, &quot;A courageous man oppresses the poor with impieties.&quot; If &quot;a poor man&quot; is retained, then the oppression would include betrayal - one would expect a poor man to have sympathy for others who are impoverished, but in fact that is not the case. It is a sad commentary on human nature that the truly oppressed people can also be oppressed by other poor people. 8 tn The comparative &quot;like&quot; does not appear in the Hebrew text, but is implied by the metaphor; it is supplied in the translation for the sake of clarity. 9 sn &quot;Food&quot; is a metonymy of effect here. The picture is of the driving rain that should cause crops to grow so that food can be produced - but does not (some English versions assume the crops are destroyed instead, e.g., NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT). The point the proverb is making is that a show of strength may not produce anything except ruin.

1 tn The idiom &quot;to harden the neck&quot; (מַקְשֶׁה־עֹרֶף, maqsheh-&apos;oref) is the idea of resisting the rebukes and persisting in obstinacy (e.g., Exod 32:9). The opposite of a &quot;stiff neck&quot; would be the bending back, i.e., submission. 2 tn The Hebrew construction is אִישׁ תּוֹכָחוֹת (&apos;ish tokhakhot, &quot;a man of rebukes&quot;), meaning &quot;a man who has (or receives) many rebukes.&quot; This describes a person who is deserving of punishment and who has been given many warnings. The text says, then, &quot;a man of rebukes hardening himself.&quot; 3 sn The stubborn person refuses to listen; he will suddenly be destroyed when the calamity strikes (e.g., Prov 6:15; 13:18; 15:10). 4 tn Or &quot;healing&quot; (NRSV).

5 tn The Hebrew form בִּרְבוֹת (birvot) is the Qal infinitive construct of רָבָה (ravah) with a בּ (bet) preposition, forming a temporal clause with a subjective genitive following it. It is paralleled in the second colon by the same construction, showing the antithesis: וּבִמְשֹׁל (uvimshol), &quot;and when the wicked rule.&quot; Some commentators wish to change the first verb to make it parallel this more closely, e.g., רָדָה (radah, &quot;to rule&quot;), but that would be too neat and is completely unsupported. The contrast is between when the righteous increase and when the wicked rule. It is not hard to see how this contrast works out in society. 6 tn The Niphal verb אָנַח (&apos;anakh) means &quot;to sigh; to groan,&quot; usually because of grief or physical and emotional distress. The word is a metonymy of effect; the cause is the oppression and distress due to evil rulers.

7 tn Heb &quot;a man.&quot; Here &quot;man&quot; is retained in the translation because the second colon mentions prostitutes. 8 tn Or &quot;causes his father to rejoice&quot;; NAB &quot;makes his father glad.&quot; 9 tn The active participle רֹעֶה (ro&apos;eh) is from the second root רָעָה (ra&apos;ah), meaning &quot;to associate with.&quot; The verb occurs only a few times, and mostly in the book of Proverbs. It is related to רֵעֶה (re&apos;eh, &quot;friend; companion; fellow&quot;). To describe someone as a &quot;companion&quot; or &quot;friend&quot; of prostitutes is somewhat euphemistic; it surely means someone who is frequently engaging the services of prostitutes. 10 tn The Hebrew verb יְאַבֶּד (yÿ&apos;abbed) means &quot;destroys&quot;; it is the Piel imperfect of the verb that means &quot;to perish.&quot; 11 sn Wealth was seen as a sign of success and of God&apos;s blessings, pretty much as it always has been. To be seen as honorable in the community meant one had acquired some substance and kept his reputation. It would be a disgrace to the family to have a son who squandered his money on prostitutes (e.g., Prov 5:10; 6:31).

1 sn This chapter has a title (30:1), Agur&apos;s confession and petition (30:2-9), and a series of Agur&apos;s admonitions (30:10-33). 2 tn The title הַמַּשָּׂא (hammasa&apos;) means &quot;the burden,&quot; a frequently used title in prophetic oracles. It may be that the word is a place name, although it is more likely that it describes what follows as an important revelation. 3 tn The definite article is used here as a demonstrative, clarifying the reference to Agur. 4 sn The word translated &quot;says&quot; (נְאֻם, nÿ&apos;um) is a verbal noun; it is also a term that describes an oracle. It is usually followed by the subjective genitive: &quot;the oracle of this man to Ithiel.&quot; 5 tn There have been numerous attempts to reinterpret the first two verses of the chapter. The Greek version translated the names &quot;Ithiel&quot; and &quot;Ukal,&quot; resulting in &quot;I am weary, O God, I am weary and faint&quot; (C. C. Torrey, &quot;Proverbs Chapter 30,&quot; JBL 73 [1954]: 93-96). The LXX&apos;s approach is followed by some English versions (e.g., NRSV, NLT). The Midrash tried through a clever etymologizing translation to attribute the works to Solomon (explained by W. G. Plaut, Proverbs, 299). It is most likely that someone other than Solomon wrote these sayings; they have a different, almost non-proverbial, tone to them. See P. Franklyn, &quot;The Sayings of Agur in Proverbs 30: Piety or Skepticism,&quot; ZAW 95 (1983): 239-52.

6 tn The particle כִּי (ki) functions in an asseverative sense, &quot;surely; indeed; truly&quot; (R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, 73, §449). 7 tn The noun בַּעַר (ba&apos;ar) means &quot;brutishness&quot;; here it functions as a predicate adjective. It is followed by מֵאִישׁ (me&apos;ish) expressing comparative degree: &quot;more than a man&quot; or &quot;more than any man,&quot; with &quot;man&quot; used in a generic sense. He is saying that he has fallen beneath the level of mankind. Cf. NRSV &quot;I am too stupid to be human.&quot; 8 tn Heb &quot;than man.&quot; The verse is using hyperbole; this individual feels as if he has no intelligence at all, that he is more brutish than any other human. Of course this is not true, or he would not be able to speculate on the God of the universe at all. 9 tn Heb &quot;the understanding of a man,&quot; with &quot;man&quot; used attributively here.

10 sn The construction uses repetition to make the point emphatically: &quot;I do not know the knowledge of the Holy One.&quot; Agur&apos;s claim to being &quot;brutish&quot; is here clarified - he is not one of those who has knowledge or understanding of God. C. H. Toy thinks the speaker is being sarcastic in reference to others who may have claimed such knowledge (Proverbs [ICC], 521). 11 tn The epithet &quot;the Holy One&quot; is the adjective &quot;holy&quot; put in the masculine plural (as in 9:10). This will harmonize with the plural of majesty used to explain the plural with titles for God. However, NRSV takes the plural as a reference to the &quot;holy ones,&quot; presumably referring to angelic beings.

1 sn Nothing else is known about King Lemuel aside from this mention in the book of Proverbs. Jewish legend identifies him as Solomon, making this advice from his mother Bathsheba; but there is no evidence for that. The passage is the only direct address to a king in the book of Proverbs - something that was the norm in wisdom literature of the ancient world (Leah L. Brunner, &quot;King and Commoner in Proverbs and Near Eastern Sources,&quot; Dor le Dor 10 [1982]: 210-19; Brunner argues that the advice is religious and not secular). 2 tn Some English versions take the Hebrew noun translated &quot;oracle&quot; here as a place name specifying the kingdom of King Lemuel; cf. NAB &quot;king of Massa&quot;; CEV &quot;King Lemuel of Massa.&quot;

3 tn The form מַה (mah), normally the interrogative &quot;what?&quot; (so KJV, ASV, NAB, NASB) is best interpreted here as an exclamation. Tg. Prov 31:2 has &quot;Woe!&quot; 4 tn In all three occurrences in this verse the word &quot;son&quot; has the Aramaic spelling, ַַבּר (bar), rather than the Hebrew בֵּן (ben). The repetition of the word &quot;son&quot; shows the seriousness of the warning; and the expression &quot;son of my womb&quot; and &quot;son of my vows&quot; are endearing epithets to show the great investment she has made in his religious place in God&apos;s program. For a view that &quot;son of my womb&quot; should be &quot;my own son,&quot; see F. Deist, &quot;Proverbs 31:1, A Case of Constant Mistranslation,&quot; JNSL 6 (1978): 1-3; cf. TEV &quot;my own dear son.&quot;

5 sn The word translated &quot;strength&quot; refers to physical powers here, i.e., &quot;vigor&quot; (so NAB) or &quot;stamina.&quot; It is therefore a metonymy of cause; the effect would be what spending this strength meant - sexual involvement with women. It would be easy for a king to spend his energy enjoying women, but that would be unwise. 6 sn The word &quot;ways&quot; may in general refer to the heart&apos;s affection for or attention to, or it may more specifically refer to sexual intercourse. While in the book of Proverbs the term is an idiom for the course of life, in this context it must refer to the energy spent in this activity. 7 tn The construction uses Qal infinitive construct לַמְחוֹת (lamkhot, &quot;to wipe out; to blot out; to destroy&quot;). The construction is somewhat strange, and so some interpreters suggest changing it to מֹחוֹת (mokhot, &quot;destroyers of kings&quot;); cf. BDB 562 s.v. מָחָה Qal.3. Commentators note that the form is close to an Aramaic word that means &quot;concubine,&quot; and an Arabic word that is an indelicate description for women.

195.content: &lt;Parabolae Salomonis.&gt;Notandum quod vulgata editio parabolas, quae Hebraice &lt;misle&gt;, Graece &lt;paraemias,&gt;id est, proverbia dicit; sed satis convenit. Quae enim parabolae quia occulta sunt nuncupantur, etiam proverbia jure vocantur: quia talia sunt, quae saepe in ore colloquentium versari ac memoria debent retineri. Etiam proverbia plerumque tam obscura sunt ut parabolae bene dicantur; unde: &lt;Haec in proverbiis locutus sum vobis&gt;Joan. 6., etc. Proverbiorum liber, non ut simplices arbitrantur, patentia habet praecepta, sed quasi in terra aurum, in nuce nucleus, in hirsutis castanearum operculis absconditus fructus inquiritur: ita in eis divinus sensus altius est inquirendus. Parabolae Salomonis secundum Hebraicam veritatem translatae ab Eusebio, Hieronymo presbytero petente Chromatio et Heliodoro episcopis; Graece, Latine &lt;similitudines;&gt;quod vocabulum ideo Salomon huic operi imposuit, ut non juxta litteram intelligamus quae dicit: in quo Dominum parabolice turbis locuturum significat, sicut et nomine suo regno pacifico, regnum Christi et Ecclesiae; de quo: &lt;Multiplicabitur ejus imperium, et regni ejus non erit finis. Super solium David, et super regnum ejus sedebit&gt;Luc. 1.. Sicut templi constructione et dedicatione, aedificationem Ecclesiae in tempore resurrectionis. Ipse etiam Christus filius David, et rex spiritualis Israel, secundum testimonium turbae, quae occurrit ei cum ramis palmarum et laudibus Matth. 21.. Quid autem utilitatis habeant, in titulo monstratur, cum dicitur: &lt;Ad sciendam sapientiam et disciplinam;&gt;id est, quomodo recte credere et vivere oporteat, quemque quo intentionem cordis dirigere.

&lt;Ad intelligenda verba prudentiae.&gt;Id est, non solum sapientiam, quam perceperunt, amplectantur, et disciplinae virtutum inserviant, sed etiam verba prudentiae, quibus proficiant, auscultent et solerter intelligant.

&lt;Audiens sapiens, sapientior.&gt;Pulchre a sapientia incipit, quia optione sibi data sapientiam petiit et accepit. &lt;Audiens sapiens, sapientior.&gt;Ostendit neminem tam sapientem in hac vita, qui non possit sapientior esse etiam dictis minorum. Audivit regina Saba Salomonem minor majorem, et sapientior rediit. Audivit Moyses socerum multo inferiorem, et sapientior factus est. &lt;Et intelligens.&gt;RAB. in Prov., tom 5. Nemo jactet se de sua scientia, etc., usque ad ad sciendam sapientiam et disciplinam, etc.
&lt;Timor Domini.&gt;ID. Duo sunt timores Domini, etc., usque ad Uterque in futuro cessabit, charitas nunquam excidet.
&lt;Audi, fili mi, disciplinam.&gt;ID. Hactenus proverbialiter, etc., usque ad apud Hebraeos enim spiritus, qui gratiam praestat, genere feminino dicitur.

&lt;Addatur gratia.&gt;His qui legem Domini servabant, etc., usque ad pro gratia rectae operationis. &lt;Et torques collo tuo,&gt;etc. Fulgor perfectae operationis, quae praedicationem quae per collum procedit, confirmet indeficienti virtutum connexione.
&lt;Fili mi.&gt;Affectu patris alloquitur filium, blandiens, ne acquiescat peccatoribus.

&lt;Insidiemur.&gt;RAB. Vel generaliter de latronibus, qui innocentibus insidias parant. Vel specialiter de illis qui vitae auctorem neci tradiderunt. STRAB. Cum generaliter ad omnes qui sanguini insidiantur hoc pertineat, etc., usque ad et se potius praesumendo perimunt. &lt;Insontem frustra.&gt;Qui peccatum non fecit, nec inventus est dolus in ore ejus.
&lt;Deglutiamus eum, sicut infernus viventem.&gt;Exstinguamus memoriam virtutum et doctrinae illius, ut etiam inter nos vixisse non memoretur.

&lt;Omnem pretiosam substantiam reperiemus.&gt;Homines, scilicet, quos Christo adhaerentes videbant, quos putabant ab ejus amore et comitatu secernere si eum occiderent, et spoliis talium domos suas replere, id est, eorum animabus sua conventicula.

&lt;Sortem mitte nobiscum.&gt;De latronibus generaliter patet, quia sociis, quos conquirunt, praedae portionem promittunt; sed et Christi persecutores, quoscunque sibi poterant, adjungebant, quos eum sequi videbant, extra synagogam faciebant, id est, sua communione privabant.
&lt;Ad malum currunt.&gt;Non solum quod facturi, sed quod pro factis passuri. Nam quanto ad facinus implendum properant, tanto ad poenam pro facinore tolerandam propinquant.
&lt;Frustra.&gt;RAB. Caetera de insidiatoribus Christi specialiter, etc., usque ad in pauperibus enim nihil habet causae.

&lt;Sapientia.&gt;Hucusque persecutiones, quas Christo Judaei intulere; hinc ea, quae per apostolos persecutoribus eisdem post passionem loquitur. &lt;Sapientia,&gt;id est Christus, loquitur &lt;foris,&gt;id est in luce palam, ut relicta infantia sint parvuli malitia. RAB. Sapientia quippe Dei Christus est, etc., usque ad cuiquam dicerent. &lt;Foris.&gt;ID. Aperte, post resurrectionem, etc., &lt;usque ad: in platea vocem ejus.&gt;&lt;In plateis dat vocem suam,&gt;etc. Quae ante paucos docuerat, manifeste replicabat, unde: &lt;Quae dico vobis in tenebris, dicite in lucem.&gt;

&lt;In capite turbarum clàmitat,&gt;etc. ID. Quia etiam principibus, qui ei praevaluisse, ut crucifigeretur, videbantur, reatum homicidii, quod perpetrarant, palam reducebat ad memoriam, eosque ad poenitentiae remedium vocabat. &lt;In foribus portarum urbis.&gt;ID. Urbs Domini, Ecclesia ex utroque populo adunata, etc., usque ad gratiam suam revocabat; ita ut, sicut Lucas ait: &lt;Multa turba sacerdotum obediret fidei&gt;Act. 6..

&lt;Usquequo. Jam&gt;Christum in carne vidistis miracula facientem, quem sprevistis: modo vel resuscitatum a morte diligite, et dimittet quod peccastis. &lt;Parvuli.&gt;RAB. Parvuli dicuntur sensu tardiores, etc., usque ad quae filius ipse veniens perfectis sensu contulit?
&lt;Convertimini.&gt;Sapientia hortatur converti ad Deum, et profert spiritum. &lt;Ad correctionem.&gt;Per apostolos Judaeos corripit, et vel post ascensionem et resurrectionem monet converti.
&lt;Ego quoque.&gt;ID. Similiter in psalmo, etc., usque ad quasi nihil contemnerent.

&lt;Cum irruerit repentina calamitas.&gt;Obsidionem Jerusalem subitam et expugnationem totius provinciae a Romanis factam dicit. De qua, &lt;Videns civitatem flevit super eam&gt;Luc. 19.. &lt;Quando venerit super vos.&gt;RAB. Potest haec tota correctio sapientiae, etc., usque ad quod enim sequitur,

&lt;Mane consurgent et non invenient me,&gt;tempus judicii significat, quo alii in vitam, alii in opprobrium resurgent sempiternum. &lt;Invocabunt.&gt;Non leguntur Judaei in obsidione Dominum invocasse; etsi qui invocaverunt, quia vere non poenituerunt, exauditi non sunt.
&lt;Exosam habuerunt.&gt;Justus econtra &lt;Iniquos,&gt;inquit, &lt;odio habui, et legem tuam dilexi.&gt;
&lt;Comedent igitur.&gt;ID. Quia vias meas ingredi noluerunt, etc., &lt;usque ad et bene tibi erit.&gt;&lt;Suisque consiliis saturabuntur.&gt;Quibus dicebant, etc., usque ad potest accipi.

&lt;Aversio.&gt;Aversio et prosperitas perdit, cum a timore conditoris aversus animus, ira ejusdem conditoris in his, quae peccat, nihil sustinere videtur adversi. Sed ut Job ait: &lt;Ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad infernum descendunt.&gt;&lt;Parvulorum.&gt;Sensu, unde supra, etc., usque ad sed quia avertunt, se interficiunt.
&lt;Qui autem me audierit, absque terrore requiescet,&gt;etc. Potest in hac vita intelligi, et in futura, etc., usque ad resurrectionis quiescet.
&lt;Fili mi.&gt;Duo hic notat, sapientiam esse de coelestibus, prudentiam de saecularibus. Abscondit mandata Dei penes se, etc., usque ad quasi semen secus viam jactatum volucres tollant.

&lt;Audiat sapientiam.&gt;Audit non aure, etc., usque ad hoc est enim quod sequitur: &lt;Inclina cor.&gt;Inclina, humilia, munda, etc., usque ad et revelasti ea humilibus. &lt;Si enim sapientiam invocaveris.&gt;Invocare, etc., usque ad nec liberum debet abesse arbitrium.
&lt;Et sicut thesauros.&gt;Qui thesauros effodit, etc., usque ad nec quiescat, donec inveniat.
&lt;Tunc intelliges.&gt;Timorem amicabilem, etc., usque ad sed etiam scientiam ipsius divinitatis quae perpetuo beatum facit invenies.

&lt;Quia Dominus dat.&gt;Respicit hic versiculus ab hoc quod supra dixerat: &lt;Si enim sapientiam invocaveris,&gt;etc. Ideo namque sapientia, etc., usque ad sed a Domino datur. &lt;Ex ore.&gt;Aeterna filii nativitate, de qua alibi: &lt;Ego ex ore Altissimi prodii, primogenita ante omnem creaturam&gt;Isai. 58.. Vel, os Domini in sanctis, unde: &lt;Os Domini locutum est.&gt;Et ex ore ejus scientia nascitur et prudentia, dum Dominus os humanum sanctificat, et suum facit, ut scienter et prudenter loquatur.

&lt;Custodiet.&gt;Ut in quocunque virtutum gradu rectos juvet et simplices. Job &lt;simplex et rectus&gt;Job. 1.; &lt;simplex,&gt;per innocentiam mansuetudinis, &lt;et rectus,&gt;per cautelam discretionis: &lt;simplex,&gt;nullum laedens, imo cunctis proficiens, &lt;rectus,&gt;a nullo corruptus.
&lt;A via mala.&gt;Ad quam vocant, qui dicunt: &lt;Veni nobiscum, insidiemur sanguini, perversa loquitur,&gt;qui est auctor hujus persuasionis.
&lt;Qui relinquunt iter.&gt;Pulchre, etc., usque ad finis ejus in tenebris exterioribus.
&lt;Qui laetantur.&gt;Quia per vias tenebrosas ambulant, etc., usque ad noxiamque laetitiam salubri fletu castigarent.
&lt;Ut eruaris a muliere.&gt;Pendet hic versus, etc., &lt;usque ad: et ipsi sunt jacula.&gt;
&lt;Et relinquit ducem.&gt;Patet et de mente haeretica, etc., usque ad quam se die baptismi servaturam promiserat.

&lt;Pacti Dei sui,&gt;etc. Quod cum viro suo tempore nuptiarum pepigit, Domino teste, quod fidem, scilicet castitatis sibi invicem servarent, vel in baptismo. &lt;Inclinata est enim.&gt;Omnis conversatio adulterae ad interitum ducit, etc., usque ad id est, ad spirituum tendit tormenta malignorum.
&lt;Ad eam non revertentur. Mortem&gt;scilicet, non mulierem, etc., usque ad non sibi attribuat, sed gratiae Dei.
&lt;Qui enim.&gt;Hic rectis jungit simplices, etc., usque ad quae cum Christo in coelis regnat, perveniunt.
&lt;Impii.&gt;De illis dicitur specialiter, etc., usque ad de fine bonorum, &lt;qui autem me audierit, absque terrore quiescet.&gt;
&lt;Fili mi, ne.&gt;Docet misericordiae operibus insistendum, etc., usque ad ornat actibus bonis, quem instruit.
&lt;Pacem,&gt;id est, statum beatitudinis, etc., usque ad longo tempore in pacis quiete viveret.

&lt;Misericordia et veritas.&gt;Ab ore tuo nunquam absit veritas dicenda, nunquam ab opere proximo misericordia impendenda: sic enim fit, ut et te Dei semper prosequatur misericordia, quae deleat peccata; veritas vero, quae compleat promissa. &lt;Circumda eas gutturi tuo.&gt;In gutture organum vocis, etc., usque ad nec voci vita contradicat.
&lt;Et invenies gratiam.&gt;Coram Domino, etc., usque ad et proximis exemplum vivendi praebeat.

&lt;Habe fiduciam in Domino.&gt;Ne metuas ob imbecillitatem tuam, etc., usque ad et quod jussit, ut implere valeas, donabit. &lt;Ne sis sapiens.&gt;Videtur idem dixisse, etc., usque ad quae sit autem vera hominis sapientia sic ostendit:
&lt;Time Deum et recede a malo.&gt;Quale est illud in Job, etc., usque ad divini timoris memoria coercet.
&lt;Sanitas quippe erit.&gt;In ossibus solida virtutum opera, etc., usque ad unde amplius roborentur, accipient.

&lt;Honora Dominum de tua substantia.&gt;Ut scilicet homines, qui ejus palma sunt, qui ad ejus imaginem facti sunt recreentur. &lt;Et de primitiis omnium.&gt;Non solum de substantia pecuniae, etc., usque ad non sibi, sed ei tribuit.

&lt;Implebuntur horrea tua saturitate. Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in coelo.&gt;Si sancti thesauros habent in coelo, etc., usque ad coelesti remuneratione, redditur. &lt;Torcularia redundabunt.&gt;Quia interna suavitas aeternorum corda cunctorum fidelium in laude sui conditoris accendit. Hic etenim dicit: &lt;Ut edatis,&gt;etc.
&lt;Disciplinam.&gt;Sunt qui in prosperis serviunt Domino, etc., usque ad pietatem, quam in tranquillitate videbatur habere, amittat.
&lt;Quem enim diligit Dominus corripit.&gt;Tanto ergo minus, etc., usque ad unde ipse ait: &lt;Ego quos amo, arguo et castigo.&gt;

&lt;Beatus homo,&gt;etc. Quia positos sub disciplina, etc., usque ad et in futuro ejus visione perfrui. &lt;Et qui affluit prudentia.&gt;Bene, cum diceret, etc., usque ad corda sua ad percipiendam ejus amplitudinem laxare.

&lt;Melior est.&gt;Non metuat de correctione inopiae, quisquis opes acquisivit sapientiae, omnibus enim thesauris munus coeleste praecellit. &lt;Primi et purissimi.&gt;Quia radix sapientiae timor Domini, hi sunt primi ac purissimi fructus, etc., usque ad a Domino perfectius promittitur.
&lt;Longitudo dierum in dextera ejus et in sinistra.&gt;Visione suae divinitatis, etc., usque ad et in futuro vitam aeternam.
&lt;Viae ejus.&gt;Actiones et doctrinae, etc., usque ad pacis et dilectionis exempla pertinent.
&lt;Lignum vitae.&gt;Sicut in medio paradisi lignum vitae, etc., usque ad praesenti beatificabitur aspectu.
&lt;Dominus sapientia.&gt;Typice, per filium Ecclesiam fidei soliditate locavit, &lt;stabilivit coelos prudentia,&gt;cum per eum sublimium praedicatorum corda illustravit.
&lt;Sapientia illius eruperunt abyssi.&gt;In diebus Noe, etc., usque ad quaeque minoribus in exemplum monstrent, examinant.
&lt;Fili mi, ne effluant.&gt;Ne disciplina temporali fatigatus, sapientiae, quae tanta est, gratiam perdas, praecave.

&lt;Et erit vita animae tuae.&gt;Habet anima tua vitam cum Deo, si ejus decreta custodieris: quamvis caro disciplina correctionis aut etiam mortis prematur. &lt;Et gratia faucibus tuis.&gt;Habet ergo sensus animi fauces suas, etc., &lt;usque ad: beatus vir qui sperat in eo.&gt;

&lt;Tunc ambulabis fiducialiter.&gt;In via nostra fiducialiter incedimus, etc., usque ad hoc est enim quod sequitur: &lt;Et pes tuus non impinget.&gt;Quoniam diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum Rom. 8..
&lt;Si dormieris, non timebis, quiesces, et suavis.&gt;Patet juxta litteram, etc., usque ad quia Deum ubique protectorem habet et custodem.

&lt;Noli prohibere benefacere eum qui.&gt;Quia supra diligenter legem Domini et consilium observare monuit, et aeternam requiem observantibus promisit: nunc multipliciter, quae observanda sunt, replicat. Primoque ad id, quod intermiserat, rediens, misericordiam proximo exhibendam, et juste, cum illo docet esse vivendum. Deinde et ab inimico cavendum esse praemonet. &lt;Noli&gt;ergo, inquit, &lt;prohibere.&gt;Ne audias a Domino cum Pharisaeis: &lt;Ipsi non introistis, et eos qui intrabant, prohibuistis&gt;Luc. 11..
&lt;Ne dicas amico tuo: Vade et revertere, cras dabo.&gt;Non solum de eleemosynis, sed de omnibus mandatis Christi, qui ait: &lt;Vos amici mei estis, si feceritis&gt;Joan. 15., etc.

&lt;Non contendas adversus hominem.&gt;Non vetat contendere adversus eum qui male facit, ut corrigatur, quia hoc frustra non fit, quod certa necessitas cogit. Imo qui ait: &lt;Si peccaverit in te frater tuus, increpa illum&gt;Matth. 18., ipse vult, ut errantem, quantum vales, ad viam veritatis reducas.

&lt;Quia abominatio Domini est omnis illusor.&gt;Omnis &lt;illusor,&gt;inquit; quia illusor est, qui vel verba Dei, quae novit, implere contemnit, vel eadem perverse intelligendo ac docendo corrumpit. Illusor est et ille, qui promissa ejus, quasi prava, despicit, ac iram districtionis, quasi tolerabilem; spernit. Necnon et ille qui proximorum simplicitati improbus insultat. Ideoque omnem hujusmodi illusorem merito divina abominatur justitia. Bene autem subditur: &lt;Et cum simplicibus sermocinatio ejus,&gt;quia superbi, dum simplicibus illudunt, prudentiores se illis, quos irrident, judicant. Sed horum prudentia, ut Jacobus ait: &lt;terrena est, animalis, diabolica&gt;Jacob. 3.. Sermocinatio autem Domini cum simplicibus est, quia illos sapientiae secretis illustrat, quos terreni fastus ac duplicitatis nihil habere considerat. Unde ait: &lt;Abscondisti haec sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis&gt;Luc. 10..

&lt;In domo impii.&gt;Ut purpurati divitis, qui in hac vita spiritualibus eguit, et post ad tantam pervenit inopiam, ut nec guttam aquae, quam quaerebat, acciperet, unde: &lt;Qui benedixit nos in omni benedictione spirituali in coelestibus in Christo, qui in remuneratione audient: Venite, benedicti,&gt;Matth. 15., etc. Sed ad litteram saepe contingit eos, qui aliena diripiunt, ad ultimum inopia consumi; at illos qui sua largiuntur, etiam bonis abundare terrenis.
&lt;Illusores.&gt;Hos versus Jacobus et Petrus juxta antiquam translationem posuerunt: &lt;Quia Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam&gt;Jacob. 4..
&lt;Audite, filii.&gt;Hinc exhortaturus ad philosophiam, qualiter ipse sapientiam sit a patre edoctus, explicat.

&lt;Nam et ego.&gt;Nihil magis ad spem percipiendae sapientiae mentes erigit, quam cum eos, quos in sapientia jam clarescere miramur, aliquando parvulos et indoctos fuisse meminimus. &lt;Unigenitus coram matre.&gt;Quare autem Salomon se &lt;unigenitum coram matre&gt;nominat, quem fratrem uterinum praecessisse Scriptura testatur, nisi quia ille mox natus sine nomine, quasi nunquam esset, de vita decessit?
&lt;Suscipiat,&gt;etc. Hujusmodi monita Salomoni a David patre data: qui Verba dierum relegit, invenit.
&lt;Posside.&gt;In omnibus quae possides, etc., usque ad juventam, venditis omnibus, comparavit.
&lt;Dabit capiti.&gt;Patet de Salomone, etc., usque ad et corona insuper vitae in futuro dabitur.
&lt;Audi, fili mi.&gt;Expositis his quae a patre acceperat, redit ad docendum auditorem sapientiam, quam coepit.
&lt;Per semitas aequitatis.&gt;Semitae, id est actiones aequitatis, etc., usque ad in viam pacis dirigentur.

&lt;Et currens.&gt;Quo amplius et alacrius ad implenda Dei mandata cucurreris, eo minus adversa, quae te impediant timebis. Nam quicunque in prava actione desudant, offendiculum in medio cursu reperiunt, quia extemplo, dum non provident, rapiuntur ad poenam.
&lt;Comedunt panem impietatis.&gt;In actione scelerum, etc., usque ad testatur Scriptura.
&lt;Justorum autem semita.&gt;Justorum opera in luce scientiae peraguntur, et aeternam ducunt ad vitam quae est perfecta dies.
&lt;Via impiorum.&gt;Dicit de his, etc., usque ad quia currens non habebit offendiculum.
&lt;Fili mi, ausculta sermones meos.&gt;Auscultandum monet sermonibus suis, et recedendum a cogitationibus pravis.
&lt;Omni custodia serva cor tuum.&gt;Sunt qui recte vivere videntur hominibus, etc., usque ad modus aestimatur vitae.

&lt;Remove a te.&gt;Duobus modis sciendum est, ut os tuum ne pravum loquatur aliquid: tua labia ne detractionibus assuescant custodias; et alios quoque, quos huic vitio subditos nosti, ne te corrumpant, fugias.
&lt;Et palpebrae.&gt;Iter justitiae, etc., usque ad meditando praevidere.
&lt;Stabilientur.&gt;Ne levitate mentis a proposito bono movearis, unde Apostolus: &lt;Stabiles estote et immobiles, abundantes in opere Domini semper&gt;I Cor. 15..

&lt;Ne declines.&gt;Dextera via bona est, etc., usque ad quod et de caeteris virtutibus et vitiis eodem modo intelligitur. &lt;Averte pedem tuum.&gt;Hoc est, ne huc vel illuc a recto devies, quia virtutes discretionem quaerunt, quarum nimietas omnis in vitio est. Si averteris a malo pedem tuum. Si bona, quae docui, Domino adjuvante, facere studueris, aderit ipse propitius conatibus tuis, ut et nunc recte ingredi, et tunc ad pacem valeas pervenire aeternam.

&lt;Fili mi, attende.&gt;Hactenus generaliter castigaverat auditorem, hinc sub specie meretricis ab haereticorum nequitia prohibet. &lt;Inclina aurem.&gt;Sapientiae inclinandam aurem, et a meretrice fugiendum, praecipue a fornicaria monet.
&lt;Labia tua.&gt;Labia, etc., usque ad vel turpia faciendo commaculat.

&lt;Favus enim.&gt;Cum in ore haeretico, etc., usque ad veritas a stultis aestimatur. &lt;Labia meretricis.&gt;Patet de meretrice, quia et sermonis suavitatem et formositatem corporis ad capiendos miseros quaerit. &lt;Oleo guttur.&gt;Oleo Spiritus sancti fides catholica consecratur: quo nitidius suum guttur ostentat, qui sua sensa patrum fide anteponit.

&lt;Novissima autem.&gt;Potio absinthii intus amarescit, etc., usque ad quare autem idem gladius &lt;biceps&gt;sit dictus, aperit Dominus cum ait: &lt;Sed eum timete qui potest animam et corpus perdere in gehennam&gt;Luc. 12..
&lt;Vagi,&gt;etc. Vagi sunt gressus haereticorum, etc., usque ad quia una eademque cunctis est agnita per totum orbem fidelibus.
&lt;Longe fac.&gt;Apostolus ait, etc., usque ad infirmis auditoribus prodest.
&lt;Ne des,&gt;etc. Ne honorem, quo ad imaginem Dei creatus es, immundorum spirituum voluntatibus subdas neque accepta vivendi spatia ad libitum adversarii crudelis expendas.
&lt;Ne forte impleantur extranei.&gt;Ne daemoniorum facta adjuves, etc., usque ad utinam lateret. &lt;Et gemas,&gt;etc. Ideo te castum custodi, etc., usque ad dicant quae sequuntur.
&lt;Cur detestatus.&gt;De haereticis specialiter patet, quia nec veterum patrum nec novorum dictis et exemplis potuerunt ab errore revocari.
&lt;In medio ecclesiae:&gt;idem est Graece, etc., usque ad alienam ab eis vitam ducere non timuit.
&lt;Bibe aquam.&gt;Docet ab haereticis cavendum et custodiae Scripturarum ac lectioni attendendum: scientiam, inquit, quam aliis praedicas, ipse serva, et tui rigatione sermonis infundere.
&lt;Deriventur.&gt;Cum ipse servaveris, tunc et aliis praedica, et in magna auditorum amplitudine divina eloquia, juxta uniuscujusque qualitatem, dispensa.

&lt;Habeto,&gt;etc. Aquas in plateis dividimus, et tamen soli habemus, quando et exterius late praedicationes fundimus, et tamen per eas laudes humanas non ambimus. &lt;Nec sint alieni.&gt;Immundi spiritus participes fiunt doctoris, si ejus mentem, vel elatione dum praedicat, vel quolibet vitio corrumpunt. &lt;Solus&gt;autem &lt;aquas possidet,&gt;cum membris Ecclesiae fideliter connexus, ab extraneis se conservat.
&lt;Sit vena.&gt;Sit doctrina tua, et quaecunque nascuntur ex ea, in benedictione Ecclesiae; et &lt;laetare cum ea, cui ab adolescentia,&gt;id est ex quo credidisti, conjunctus es.

&lt;Cerva charissima.&gt;Vel &lt;gratissima,&gt;ut quidem codices habent, sancta est Ecclesia, etc., &lt;usque ad,&gt;contra haereticorum fraudes instruimur. &lt;Amore,&gt;etc. Non uxorio amori insistere docet; sed ne prima vivente aliam ducas, vel meretrici unquam socieris.
&lt;Respicit Dominus.&gt;Non se putent adulteri noctis tenebris, etc., &lt;usque ad: et nox sicut dies illuminabitur.&gt;
&lt;Iniquitates,&gt;etc. Peccator, etc., usque ad quam quo se arctius obligent, agunt.
&lt;Ipse morietur.&gt;Quia de adulteris, etc., usque ad quia disciplinam vitae detestati sunt.
&lt;Fili mi.&gt;Litteraliter patet, etc., usque ad teipsum prius necesse est, quae dixeris, custodire.
&lt;Suscita.&gt;Non tantum ipse bene vivendo vigilare memento, sed illum, cui praees, a peccati torpore praedicando suscita.
&lt;Ne dederis&gt;somnum oculis, etc., usque ad sed haec propter mentis taedium digna invectione non corrigit.
&lt;Eruere.&gt;Quasi dicat: Velut damula de manu captantis, etc., usque ad et coelestis vitae pascua merearis intrare.
&lt;Vade ad formicam.&gt;Hinc vacantem hortatur, etc., usque ad de horreo priscae actionis quod recondidit proferre.
&lt;Usquequo, piger, dormies, quando.&gt;Usquequo, piger, dormies in vitiis, etc., usque ad hoc est enim quod sequitur, et &lt;veniet tibi quasi viator.&gt;
&lt;Egestas, et paupertas.&gt;Patet juxta litteram, etc., usque ad quia improvisa et subitanea. &lt;Si vero impiger.&gt;Fructus terreni, etc., usque ad quia mercedem laborum indeficientem percipiet.
&lt;Homo apostata.&gt;Dixerat de haeresi et aliis vitiorum generibus, etc., usque ad quod nulla interius radice subsistat.

&lt;Sex sunt.&gt;De eodem quam sit odibilis Deo seminando discordiam insinuat. &lt;Detestatur anima.&gt;Secundum consuetudinem hominum loquitur, ut eum valde tales odisse significet, unde in Isaia: &lt;Solemnitates vestras odivit anima mea&gt;Isa. 1..
&lt;Oculos,&gt;etc. Enumerat sex capitalia crimina, etc., usque ad qui concordiam fraternae unitatis sciderunt.
&lt;Conserva, fili.&gt;Nunc sub adulterae mulieris specie prohibet ab auditione haereseos.
&lt;Liga ea in corde,&gt;id est, in cogitatione praecepta Dei fixa tene.

&lt;Cum ambulaveris.&gt;Tanta sit meditatio divinae legis, etc., &lt;usque ad: gradiantur tecum mandata Dei, ut te instruant.&gt;&lt;Cum dormieris:&gt;in morte custodiant animam tuam, ne rapiat hostis. Cum evigilaveris in resurrectione, loquere cum eis exspectando praemia, quae tibi, si ea servasses, promissa erant.
&lt;Non concupiscat.&gt;Patet de adultera, sed haeretici si bene vivere et apte se agere videntur, vide ne seducaris eorum doctrinis.
&lt;Pretium enim scorti.&gt;Brevis voluptas fornicationis, etc., usque ad sed post paululum ardentior redit.
&lt;Nunquid potest homo abscondere ignem.&gt;Soli ei conceditur haereticorum libros legere, qui adeo solidatus est in fide catholica, ut verborum dulcedine vel astutia nequeat ab ea separari.
&lt;Non grandis est culpa.&gt;Furtum non ex se, etc., usque ad sed quia Jerusalem plura commisit.
&lt;Quia zelus et furor viri non,&gt;etc. Et de Domino intelligendum est, etc., usque ad sive animam quamque fidelem corrumpere praesumit.
&lt;Fili mi.&gt;Haec periocha eadem quae superior plenius explicat.
&lt;Et legem meam.&gt;Tam solerter serva, quae doceo, quasi nil recti sine his aspicias.
&lt;Dic sapientiae, soror.&gt;Sapientiam ecclesiasticae doctrinae sororia tibi dilectione conjunge, ut haec te a pollutione servet haeretica, quae a vera castitate Ecclesiae probatur extranea.
&lt;De fenestra.&gt;Patet juxta litteram, etc., usque ad quia deseruit angustam viam quae ducit ad vitam.
&lt;Juxta angulum,&gt;quia deflectit a rectitudine; et &lt;prope viam domus illius graditur:&gt;quia a via veritatis declinavit, merito viae domus meretricis vel haeretici appropiat.
&lt;In obscuro advesperascente.&gt;Quia jam talis per caecitatem cordis, ad tenebras festinat peccati et damnationis.
&lt;Et ecce mulier occurrit ornatu illi meretricio.&gt;Patent haec cuncta, etc., usque ad spirituali morte perimit.
&lt;Nec valens in domo.&gt;Nulla est haeresis, quae primis contenta sit discipulis hi enim sunt domus ejus, sed semper novos, quos decipiat quaerit.

&lt;Apprehensumque deosculatur juvenem,&gt;id est, falsorum verborum blandimentis tentat instabilem. &lt;Et procaci vultu blanditur, dicens:&gt;Juxta litteram patet, etc., usque ad nam et Dominus ad discipulos: &lt;Sed venit hora, ut omnis qui interficit vos,&gt;etc. Joan. 16..
&lt;Intexui funibus lectulum.&gt;Solent lecti, etc., usque ad per quam haeretica mens sensum doctrinae pestilentis, quasi meretrix thorum facinoris, se texuisse gloriatur.
&lt;Aspersi cubile meum.&gt;Promittunt se tales odorem coelestium habere virtutum, quibus sua suorumque corda, velut funibus cubilia venusta, consecrantur, quasi, Christi bonus odor sumus Deo.
&lt;Veni, inebriemur uberibus.&gt;Doctrinae sanctae poculis se invicem satiandos jactant haeretici, et virtutum gratia conjungendos, donec eorum gesta lux sequatur aeterna.
&lt;Sacculum pecuniae secum tulit.&gt;Gloriam resurrectionis, immortalitatis decus, quo illius patriae cives laetificaret et ditaret.
&lt;Et fortissimi quique interfecti sunt ab ea.&gt;Ut ipse Salomon sapientissimus, etc., usque ad qui negaverit errat.

&lt;Viae inferi domus ejus, penetrantes.&gt;Sed de Ecclesia Dominus ait: &lt;Portae inferi non praevalebunt adversus eam&gt;Matth. 16.. &lt;Interiora mortis.&gt;Obscuriora et arctiora gehennae tormenta, quibus haereticos et fornicatores constat esse mergendos.
&lt;Nunquid non sapientia,&gt;etc. Dominus palam locutus est mundo: et in occulto locutus est nihil. Quid ergo neglecto Evangelio ejus, ad haeresim et lasciviam miseri confluunt?
&lt;In summis,&gt;etc. In monte discipulos simul et turbas docuit, etc, usque ad qui contra eum in occulto loquuntur?
&lt;O viri, ad vos.&gt;Ad viros clamat, id est ad strenuos verbi auditores: in utroque sexu namque feminae, id est, fluxae mentes sapientiae verba percipere nequeunt.
&lt;Intelligite, parvuli,&gt;etc. Manifestum est de Domino, etc., usque ad quos seducere valeat, quaerit.
&lt;Labia mea.&gt;Duo testamenta, etc., usque ad ad praedicandum salutem universum aperta per orbem.
&lt;Arrogantiam.&gt;Arrogantiam et superbiam in eis, etc., usque ad sed juxta auditorum libitum sua verba commutant.
&lt;Meum est consilium.&gt;Non se extollat humana praesumptio: plenitudinem virtutum sola Dei sapientia possidet, ab hac humana infirmitas, quidquid habet virtutis, accipit.
&lt;Per me reges.&gt;Reges dicit apostolos, etc., usque ad ait enim: &lt;Sine me nihil potestis facere&gt;Joan. 15..

&lt;Ego diligentes,&gt;etc. &lt;Qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre: et ego diligam eum, et manifestabo ei meipsum&gt;Joan. 14.. &lt;Mane&gt;quippe ad sapientiam &lt;vigilant,&gt;qui innovato mentis studio ad Christi visionem attingere satagunt.
&lt;Mecum sunt divitiae.&gt;Opes superbas, opes excelsas dicit, etc., usque ad et promissa ipsius exspectamus in quibus est justitia.

&lt;Dominus possedit me.&gt;Hucusque locutus est parabolice ad Filium, nunc vero quia mentionem fecerat de sapientia, et non dixerat quae esset, et quantae dignitatis, quasi incidenter ostendit et commendat eam secundum utramque naturam, scilicet divinam et humanam, dicit &lt;Dominus,&gt;etc. Viae Domini sunt opera, etc., usque ad caro enim ejus propter opera, divinitas ante opera.
&lt;Ludens in orbe.&gt;Quia cum tempora et creaturae orbis terrae coepissent, ipse, quod erat, in Patre Filius manebat: hoc ideo, ne quis eum cum creaturis et temporibus esse prohiberet.
&lt;Ad fores.&gt;Scripturas, vel doctores; iidem et postes, sine quibus ad vitam, quam pollicetur, non valemus ingredi.

&lt;Sapientia aedificavit.&gt;Quia de aeternitate divinitatis Christi sufficienter dixerat, etc., usque ad quia ab amore saeculi disjunctos ad portandam Ecclesiae fabricam erexit. &lt;Columnas septem.&gt;Scilicet Ecclesias per orbem, etc., usque ad quasi sustentando continerent.
&lt;Venite, comedite panem meum.&gt;In unam Christi personam junctam divinitatem et humanitatem, vel, in &lt;pane&gt;corpus, in &lt;vino&gt;sanguis ejus, quo in altari satiamur.
&lt;Relinquite.&gt;Post oblatas epulas addit et vitae monita, ut quos perceptis suae incarnationis mysteriis reficit, doctrinae pariter instruat verbis.
&lt;Qui erudit,&gt;etc. Quasi interrogares, etc., usque ad et majorem credens.
&lt;Noli arguere.&gt;Non est timendum, etc., usque ad sed dilectionis ejus gratia cessandum.
&lt;Si sapiens.&gt;Moneo te ad sapientiam, quod tamen tibi prodest, non mihi. Si enim &lt;sapiens fueris,&gt;etc.

&lt;Mulier stulta.&gt;Superius commendavit sapientiam per divinitatem et humanitatem, nunc per contrarium illam eamdem commendabiliorem ostendit, ubi &lt;mulier stulta,&gt;etc., quae est ei contraria, &lt;sedet,&gt;etc. &lt;Mulier,&gt;etc. Mulier hic haeresis est, etc., usque ad haec in supercilio mentis attollitur.
&lt;Qui est parvulus.&gt;Sapientia parvulos atque insipientes, etc., usque ad et ad se divertere.
&lt;Aquae furtivae.&gt;Sapientia palam mensam omnibus proposuit, etc., usque ad prohibita et illicita connubia dulciora esse asseverat.
&lt;Et ignoravit quod ibi.&gt;Nescit mulier adultera, etc., usque ad et in excelsis coelorum convivae fidelium.

&lt;Parabolae Salomonis.&gt;Novum ponit titulum, quia novum genus locutionis incipit, scilicet, ut non, sicut prius, de singulis bonorum malorumve partibus diutius disputet; sed alternis versibus actus utrorumque describat. &lt;Filius sapiens.&gt;Qui accepta fidei mysteria bene servat, laetificat Deum Patrem; qui vero haec actione mala vel haeresi commaculat, matrem contristat Ecclesiam.
&lt;Nil proderunt.&gt;Et a transitoria morte, etc., usque ad quod pro vita sunt dati, conferunt.
&lt;Non affliget Dominus.&gt;Et si aliquando, etc., usque ad juste vindicando, retorquet.
&lt;Egestatem operata.&gt;Qui negligenter vivit in hoc saeculo, egebit bonis in futuro; at qui fortiter Domino militant, divitiis aeternae beatitudinis remunerantur.

&lt;Qui congregat.&gt;Qui congregat Christo animas fidelium, filius sapiens est. Et quidem haec &lt;messis multa est, operarii vero pauci&gt;Matth. 9.. Qui vero hoc tempore acceptabili a sua salute curanda torpescit, confundetur in die tribulationis.

&lt;Os autem impiorum.&gt;Quod comessationi, ebrietati et colloquiis malis serviebat, propter iniquitatem, quam congessit, condemnabitur. Denique &lt;os&gt;illius &lt;iniquitas operuit&gt;qui in tormentis positus in lingua sibi, in qua ob plura scelera plus punitus est, refrigerium quaesivit.
&lt;Memoria.&gt;In hac vita boni bonos, etc., usque ad et ignis eorum non exstinguetur.

&lt;Stultus ceditur labiis,&gt;vel suis, quibus damnari meruit, quia &lt;mors et vita in manibus linguae&gt;Isa. 66., vel eorum a quibus, quia corrigi non potuit, sententiam damnationis accepit; unde: &lt;Domine, libera animam meam a labiis iniquis&gt;Psal. 119..
&lt;Qui ambulat,&gt;qui simpliciter se vivere novit, etc., usque ad ac digna factis recipit, &lt;nihil enim occultum quod non reveletur&gt;Matth. 10..
&lt;Virga in dorso ejus.&gt;Vindicta in sequenti vita, etc., usque ad recte subditur: &lt;Sapientes abscondunt,&gt;etc.

&lt;Substantia divitis.&gt;Spiritualiter: Qui in Deum dives est per bona opera, confidit in illo, quasi qui in urbe inexpugnabili, quae a nullo hoste possit superari; at, qui virtutum inopia coangustantur, ideo coelestibus egent divitiis, quia noxio pavore timent duros pro Domino tolerare labores.

&lt;Abscondunt scientiam,&gt;etc. Si ergo verax et sapiens esse desideras, odium neque in abscondito cordis conteges, neque per oris contumeliam proferas; sed tuum cor dilectione et os veritate repleatur.

&lt;Quasi per risum stultus operatur scelus.&gt;Prudentia a providendo nomen accepit. Stultus est igitur qui gaudet in scelere. Sapientis autem est et ejus qui viri nomine dignus sit, praevidere, quia risus dolore miscebitur, et gaudia peccandi poena sequetur ultionis.
&lt;Quod timet impius, veniet super.&gt;De illo impio dicit, etc., usque ad quod corde tenent, adveniet.
&lt;Quasi tempestas.&gt;De persecutoribus Ecclesiae dicit, qui domum fidei subvertere quaerunt. Sed illa in vero fundamento, id est, in Christo collocata, ipsi extemplo dispereunt.
&lt;Sicut acetum dentibus.&gt;Sicut haereticorum perfidia, etc., usque ad et etiam verbis impugnant, unde: &lt;A nobis exierunt, sed ex nobis non erant&gt;I Joan. 2..
&lt;Spes autem.&gt;Non contra id quod supra dicitur, etc., usque ad De his qui scienter delinquunt, adjungit.
&lt;Fortitudo simplicis via ejus, et pavor.&gt;Si obscura Scripturarum, etc., usque ad operari contemnunt.
&lt;Statera dolosa.&gt;Vel pecuniae vel judicii, etc., usque ad et actioni congruit.
&lt;Ubi fuerit superbia.&gt;Superbi, vel contumeliose se gerunt per contemptum sive per ignorantiam disciplinae, vel proximis contumeliam ingerunt, vel qui se exaltat humiliabitur.

&lt;Mortuo homine impio.&gt;Hoc Origenes nescivit, etc., usque ad et ad eos fortasse pertinet quod sequitur. &lt;Exspectatio sollicitorum.&gt;Sollicitudo bonorum est implere Dei praecepta; at malorum scienter peccantium, quod aeternam rapientur ad poenam. Ideoque exspectatio illorum coronabitur; istorum damnabitur, etiam ante judicium, damuante propria conscientia.
&lt;Simulator.&gt;Haereticus simulans catholicam doctrinam, decipit auditorem suum. Qui veritatem sequuntur Evangelii liberabuntur sapientia catholica, ne decipula decipiantur haeretica.

&lt;Qui despicit,&gt;etc. Non est despiciendus, qui nos simpliciter amat, etsi quid inepte agat: qui enim hoc facit, indiget sapientia. Prudens autem publice tacet, occulte castigat, quod melius in sequentibus aperitur.
&lt;Ubi non est gubernator, populus corruet, salus autem ubi multa consilia.&gt;Ne enim putares, etc., usque ad ut a pluribus corrigatur.

&lt;Affligetur.&gt;Ad litteram patet, etc., usque ad seipsum ante districti judicis oculos ultione dignum reddet. &lt;Qui autem cavet laqueos securus erit.&gt;Securus erit in futuro qui nunc bene formidolosus et sua peccata per poenitentiam curat, et ab impoenitentium societate se immunem servat.
&lt;Manus in manu.&gt;Qui manum jungit in manu, etc., usque ad unde praemissum est: &lt;Abominabile Domino cor pravum.&gt;
&lt;Circulus aureus in naribus,&gt;etc. Si suis naribus circulum auri fixeris, etc., usque ad quia carnalibus deditus.

&lt;Bene consurgit diluculo qui quaerit bona,&gt;etc., id est ad vitam consurgit in tempore resurrectionis, quia nunc bona agit in tempore operationis. Qui autem mala, quae dicat vel agat, inquirit, eorum pondere ab altioribus retardatur.

&lt;Justi autem quasi,&gt;etc. Quasi, qui spe futurorum praemiorum bona faciunt in praesenti, juste, quod sperant, accipiunt. Virens quippe in arbore folium, fructus, quos nondum ostendit, signat affuturos: et justi quasi virens folium germinant, qui spe salvi facti in fidei ac virtutum gratia proficere non cessant.
&lt;Qui stultus est.&gt;Impius vivit pio; ille damnatur, iste accipit bravium, pro quo certabat.
&lt;Qui suscipit.&gt;Qui animarum curam pro Domino suscipit, etc., usque ad ut sublimius cum Domino regnet, procurat.
&lt;Si justus.&gt;Si martyres tanta patiuntur injuste, etc., usque ad etsi enim impii non sumus, certe si peccatores nos esse negamus, &lt;nosipsos seducimus, et veritas in nobis non est.&gt;

&lt;Qui bonus est,&gt;etc. Horum versiculorum connexio talis est; qui bonus est non confidit in cogitationibus suis; sed Domini gratiam quaerit, ac per illam pie vivit. Qui autem in cogitationibus suis confidit, bonus esse nequit: qui enim gratiam Dei non curat quaerere, in prava actione perdurat.
&lt;Mulier.&gt;Ad litteram, mulier bona et casta, etc., usque ad putredo pravi dogmatis corrumpit.
&lt;Cogitationes.&gt;Justi sua facta, etc., usque ad obliti timoris Domini.
&lt;Verte impios.&gt;Multa impietas in diis gentium, etc., usque ad sed quaecunque membra hinc illuc perveniunt, quae sperabant, gaudia inveniunt.

&lt;Novit,&gt;id est compatitur hebetudini ac fragilitati proximorum sibi commissorum. &lt;Viscera autem impiorum crudelia,&gt;qui non compatiuntur subditis; sed sicut Dominus ait: &lt;Percutiunt pueros et ancillas,&gt;dicentes: &lt;Moram facit Dominus meus venire.&gt;

&lt;Desiderium.&gt;Desiderat impius, etc., usque ad dicit e contra de bonis. &lt;Radix autem justorum proficiet,&gt;fides, spes, charitas, quibus in Christo sunt radicati non eos fallunt; sed plus quam sperant in futuro percipient.

&lt;Fatuus,&gt;etc. Qui in praesenti desiderat ulcisci, fatuus est; qui autem pro Domino contemnit, sapiens est. &lt;Qui autem dissimulat:&gt;non sic vult occultari, ut duret, sed omnino deleatur; est enim natura irae ut prolata, magis ferveat; occultata, languescat.
&lt;Lingua autem sapientium est sanitas,&gt;etc., quia et bona, quae promittunt, ipsi perficiendo ad vitam perveniunt; et aliis, quae sequantur, demonstrant
&lt;Labium veritatis,&gt;etc. Fides catholica semper permanebit; qui autem repente nova dogmata inserit, mendacii minister est.

&lt;Homo versutus.&gt;Sapiens et prudens: qui aliquando celat scientiam, vel non valens loqui, quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnalibus; vel nolens dare sanctum canibus, vel margaritas ante porcos projicere, vel mittere. &lt;Cor insipientium provocat.&gt;Vel quando plus appetunt sapere quam oportet sapere, et in cogitationibus evanescendo, pro sapientia stultitiam habent et tenent; vel aliis, quae nequeunt capere, ingerentes, quasi infirmis oculis lumen solis, id est sapientiae, quam habere videbantur auferunt.

&lt;Manus fortium.&gt;Perfecti non solum vitiorum bella superant, sed et electis fratribus majore virtutum gratia principantur. &lt;Quae autem remissa.&gt;Qui dissoluti animo, etc., usque ad non enim de talibus desperandum est, cum adjungit, &lt;moeror justi,&gt;etc.

&lt;Maeror in corde,&gt;etc., quia necesse est ut prius peccatorem moeror poenitentiae salubriter humiliet, et post per judicium sacerdotis datae reconciliationis sermo laetificet vel reficiat. &lt;Qui negligit damnum,&gt;etc. Si hoc ad litteram accipitur, etc., usque ad vel ipsam carnem morti tradit?
&lt;Non inveniet,&gt;etc. Fraude namque acquisita pecunia, etc., usque ad quibus aeternae vitae claritas auro pretiosior emitur.
&lt;Filius sapiens.&gt;Tantum distat inter sapientem et stultum, ut hic aliquando profectu eruditionis ad eum, qui se docuerat, docendum perveniat: ille, ne, cum arguitur, audiat.

&lt;Vult et non vult piger.&gt;Vult regnare cum Domino, etc., usque ad et Jesus filius Sirach: &lt;Vae peccatori terram duabus viis ingredienti.&gt;&lt;Anima autem operantium&gt;jussa dominica &lt;impinguabitur,&gt;quia perfecta supernorum dulcedine reficietur; unde: &lt;Sicut adipe&gt;Psal. 26., etc.; vel, qui piis pro Domino laboribus insudant, immarcescibili corona donabuntur.
&lt;Est quasi dives,&gt;non vere, ut qui induebatur purpura et bysso Luc. 16.; sed quia Deum non habuit, etc., usque ad quid vera paupertas agat, subditur.
&lt;Substantia,&gt;etc. Qui volunt divites fieri incidunt in tentationem, etc., usque ad multiplicia supernae beatitudinis munera percipiet, de quo:
&lt;Spes quae differtur,&gt;etc. Quia nimirum, etc., usque ad ipse est enim &lt;lignum vitae amplectentibus se.&gt;
&lt;Qui detrahit.&gt;Aliter, etc., usque ad unde: &lt;Si praeoccupatus fuerit homo in aliquo delicto,&gt;etc.
&lt;Lex sapientis.&gt;Ex quo homo sapere incipit, utitur hac lege, ut mortem vitet et vitam acquirat.
&lt;Cum consilio,&gt;maxime divino, quod est in Scripturis. Fatuus enim est qui extra hoc consilium vivit, quamvis naturaliter prudens videatur.

&lt;Qui cum sapientibus.&gt;Quilibet simplex aut rusticus, qui arcana sapientiae comprehendere nequit, si tamen exempla sapientum vivendo sectatur, jure inter sapientes numerabitur. &lt;Amicus stultorum.&gt;Qui stultos, non quia homines sunt, sed propter stultitiam, quia mimi sunt, vel histriones, vel hujusmodi, non ut instruendo corrigat, amat, sed ut favendo, deteriores efficiat: licet sapiens videatur, stultorum damnatione tenebitur.
&lt;Bonus homo,&gt;etc., saepe boni sine filiis obeunt, etc., usque ad regnum Dei datum est genti facienti fructum ejus.
&lt;Multi cibi.&gt;Alius translator, etc., usque ad utrique autem sensui congruit, quod subdit.
&lt;Qui parcit virgae odit filium suum,&gt;etc. Nam et bonus pater filium, et discipulum magister catholicus, ne ad iniquitatem deflectat, sollicitus erudit.
&lt;Sapiens,&gt;etc. &lt;Destruet&gt;male vivendo, et aliquando aperte regnando, etc., usque ad de quibus aperte subdit:
&lt;In ore stulti.&gt;Quia stulti per vaniloquium humiles, quos despiciunt, affligunt; sed hi per doctrinam sapientium, ne decipiantur, se muniunt.
&lt;Ubi non,&gt;etc. Haec haerent superioribus, etc., usque ad qui Sareptanam viduam pascit a qua et ipse pascitur.
&lt;Quaerit derisor sapientiam,&gt;etc. Ut Caiphas, etc., usque ad quia perverse quaerunt, nunquam prorsus inveniunt.
&lt;Vade contra,&gt;etc. Ideo derisor sapientiam, quam quaerit, non invenit, etc., usque ad ejusque meditationi operam dare satagunt.

&lt;Extraneus.&gt;Id est reprobus, etc., usque ad unde subditur: &lt;Dominus impiorum,&gt;etc. &lt;Sapiens timet et declinat.&gt;Sicut stulti est de sua alacritate confidere, etc., usque ad aut post mortem fortiter poenas ferat.
&lt;Impatiens,&gt;etc. Reprehensibilis quidem est impatiens, etc., usque ad inter reprobos aestimatur.
&lt;Jacebunt mali ante bonos.&gt;Videntes tormenta eorum, etc., usque ad ad videnda eorum supplicia.
&lt;Fatuitas stultorum.&gt;Imprudentia, quasi improvidentia dicitur.

&lt;Liberat animas testis fidelis.&gt;Catholicus praedicatur, qui testimonia Scripturarum fideliter praedicat, et profert; haereticus mendacia. &lt;Profert mendacia.&gt;Alia translatio: Incendit autem mendacio animas dolosus deceptor. &lt;Versipellis,&gt;id est diabolus, qui mala, quae suggerit, bona mentitur: et dum bona promittit aeterna, ducit ad tormenta.
&lt;In timore Domini.&gt;Timor Domini fiduciam fortitudinis praestat, etc., usque ad speraverunt in Domino.
&lt;Timor Domini.&gt;Haec est spes eorum, etc., usque ad unde, &lt;Initium sapientiae timor Domini&gt;Psal. 9..

&lt;Vita carnium.&gt;Per carnem infirma, per ossa firma. Si mentis innocentia custoditur, etsi quae foris infirma sunt, quandoque roborantur; unde subdit: &lt;Putredo ossium invidia,&gt;quia per livoris vitium ante oculos Dei pereunt ea quae humanis oculis fortia videntur. Ossa enim per invidiam putrescere, est robusta quaeque perire.
&lt;Responsio mollis frangit iram.&gt;Qui verba increpantis humiliter suscipit, jam propinquat veniae reatus quem gessit. Qui arguenti resultat, contra se iram judicis provocat.

&lt;Ebullit stultitiam.&gt;Scripturam pervertendo, suos sensus auctoritati praeponendo; velut fatui philosophi, ut Porphyrius, et Julianus, qui contra Ecclesiae doctores stultitiae suae fluenta fundebant.
&lt;Stultus irridet.&gt;Stultus est omnis peccator, qui, terrenis actibus deditus, futurum nihil praevidet: is disciplinam irridet, dum derogat divinae correctioni.
&lt;Cor stultorum dissimile.&gt;Vel dissimile sibi ipsi, variis cogitationibus, et nunquam idem manet. Contra quod de Anna dicitur: &lt;Vultusque ejus non sunt amplius in diversa mutati.&gt;

&lt;Doctrina mala. Qui solverit unum de mandatis istis minimis, et docuerit sic homines, minimus est in regno coelorum.&gt;Talibus tamen, si correcti fuerint, patet reditus ad veniam: si autem increpationes non receperint, omnino morientur.
&lt;Omnes dies.&gt;Omne tempus populi Dei, etc., usque ad quasi jugi delectantur convivio.
